description.narrative: The Australia-Indonesia Knowledge Partnership Platform (KONEKSI) is the Australian Government's program in the knowledge and innovation sector in Indonesia. The program's goal is to achieve enduring relationships between Australian and Indonesian institutions that advance mutual interest and support Indonesia's inclusive and sustainable development. KONEKSI supports partnerships between various institutions in Australia and Indonesia to find innovative policy and technological solutions on issues of shared interests such as climate change, digital transformation, bioeconomy and energy transition. KONEKSI supports competitive research grants, technical assistance to build GoI’s capability in R&D and Innovation, build networks and coalitions, and knowledge management and dissemination. KONEKSI advances people-to-people and institutional links between Australia and Indonesian organizations in research, science, technology, and innovation.

description.narrative: Australia assisted 25 Indonesian organisations for people with disabilities (OPDs) to develop research skills including applying inclusive research methodologies that drives better outcomes for gender and disabilities. Collaborating with SAPDA, an Indonesian disability rights organisation, Australia established a ‘Research School’ tailored to persons with disabilities. The Research School will enhance capacity of 25 OPDs on tools and techniques for disability-inclusive research and generate networking opportunities for individual researchers. Graduates will be able to develop compelling research proposals, identify fit for purpose methods, and actively participate in local and international network of researchers. In addition, Australia provided grant funding to enable a further 3 OPDs to complete research projects highlighting climate adaptation and resilience of vulnerable community groups in eastern Indonesia, in partnership with Australian universities and research organisations

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: Australia established 38 partnerships between 111 Indonesian and Australian organisations to generate solutions to address climate change. ‍ These collaborative research projects address a wide variety of climate change-related issues including adaptation, resilience, and future proofing. For example, a project in Central Java has successfully trialled the use of AI to predict increasingly frequent coastal flooding events, improving response time. Another innovative project in East Nusa Tenggara has co-created an interactive game that engages school-age children in learning about and responding to climate change risks using local knowledge. The Ministry of Education, Culture, Research and Technology is considering replicating the use of the game through national curriculum. ‍ Through these collaborative research projects, Australia has worked in partnership with Indonesia to make a substantial contribution to policy and innovation agenda. According to Indonesia’s research, science and innovation agency (BRIN), Australia was Indonesia’s number one research partners in 2023.

Australia, through KONEKSI, supported the partnership between Indonesian disability rights organisation (OPD) SAPDA and the Australian OPD Christian Blind Mission (CBM) to co-design and launch the Disability Research School. It is an online/offline collaboration platform to strengthen research capacity, leadership, knowledge sharing, peer-to-peer networks, while advancing inclusive research methodologies grounded in lived experiences of people with disabilities. The partnership facilitated a valuable exchange of technical expertise on inclusive research practices, including research grant management, curriculum development, and co-production of tailored learning modules on inclusive research methodologies–delivered by and for researchers with disabilities. ‍ Through this initiative, the KONEKSI-SAPDA Disability Research School reached 107 national and local OPDs across Indonesia. Of these 107 OPDs network, 21 OPDs also received intensive classes on Inclusive Research Methodology and GEDSI (Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion) perspectives in research. ‍ This initiative strengthens the long-term capacity of OPDs in Indonesia to lead and participate meaningfully in the research to promote and to advocate the rights of people with disabilities. It also ensures disability-inclusive development is prioritised in the strategic policy processes. In the future, this support could position SAPDA as a leading OPD in Indonesia for inclusive research.

title.narrative: Climate adaptation, mitigation, environment and biodiversity

description.narrative: In Jepara, Central Java, seawater intrusion is contaminating freshwater aquifers, reducing the availability of clean water for local communities. Through KONEKSI, Australia provided collaborative research grant to the Australian National University (ANU) and Universitas Diponegoro (UNDIP) to develop and install a solar-powered, energy-efficient desalination plant. The system addresses the global challenge of high energy use in desalination, with its per-unit water production cost comparing favourably to similar plants in Australia, Jordan, Tunisia and the United States. ‍ In March 2025, the Government of Indonesia officially certified the water quality from the plant as safe for drinking. With additional funding from the private sector, the plant is now fully operational and produces approximately 4,000 litres of potable water per day. It supplies clean water to around 250 households in affordable housing communities in Slamaran and nearby areas of Jepara. ‍ The project has gained strong interest from local media and policymakers, received endorsement from Central Java’s newly elected governor, and secured 2026 operational funding from the Jepara district government. Furthermore, the use of solar power as the plant’s main source of energy contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, which in turn will indirectly contribute to Indonesia’s pathways towards 2060 net-zero emissions.
